answer: Make each seat prove it stores its own sealed replica of a public archive. The archive is re-encoded with a slow, sequential seal keyed to that seat's identity, so copies can't be shared or deduplicated, and a gale of random spot reads must be answered within seconds, too fast to reseal on demand. A farm of hollow seats then needs a full canyon of disk per identity, so its cost grows linearly while each honest agent pays once.
